title: Missed Call Text Back: video sales letter

slides.title: It's 9 PM. The *phone rings*. *Nobody answers.*
slides.sub: What one unanswered call can cost a home service company
slides.narration: It's nine at night. A homeowner has water coming through the ceiling. They call the first plumber they find online. It rings, and rings. Nobody picks up. Many callers won't leave a voicemail. They call the next company on the list. And just like that, a job is gone before anyone knew it existed.

slides.title: What was on the *other end* of that call?
slides.note: Examples of large jobs by trade. Actual job values and outcomes vary.
slides.narration: That call was not a two hundred dollar service visit. It could have been a twelve thousand dollar repipe. A fifteen thousand dollar H V A C system. A thirty thousand dollar roof. Or a hundred thousand dollar water loss job. The biggest jobs often come at the worst times, from people who need an answer right now.

slides.title: Why calls get missed

cards.p: Under a sink, on a roof, or with another customer.
Dinner, family time, or asleep at two in the morning.

slides.narration: You can't be everywhere. You're under a sink, on a roof, or with another customer. Or you're finally having dinner. Even companies with a team answering the phones around the clock still miss calls. No one can pick up every call.
